Class Harness

java.lang.Object
org.nasdanika.sdk.runtime.harness.Harness
public final class Harness extends Object
Runs code against an HTTP server that is up only while the code runs, in one trace: the code runs in a span, requests it sends through the Server are client spans that carry the trace to the server, and every request the server handles is a server span, a child of the client span that sent it. 
String body = Harness.inServer("Library", routes -> routes.createContext("/", handler), server -> {
    return server.get("/books").body();
});
Like Telemetry.inSpan(io.opentelemetry.api.trace.Tracer, String, Attributes, Telemetry.SpanBody), with a server around the body. The server listens on the loopback address on a free port and handles requests on virtual threads; every context created on it is instrumented with TelemetryHandler. It is stopped when the body returns or throws.

The telemetry goes to the OpenTelemetry given, or the current one. With one instance for the client and the server, which is what running both in one JVM gives for free, the client's and the server's spans are in one trace and one recording.

      Starts a server, configures it, runs the body in a span with the server's address as attributes, and stops the server.
      Parameters:
      openTelemetry - Receives the spans of the body, its requests and the server
      name - Name of the span the body runs in
      routes - Creates the server's contexts. Contexts are instrumented as they are created
      body - Runs while the server is up

      What the body returns
